law.title: Finance Act 2025, section 51: Increased rates for additional dwellings: transactions on or after 1 April 2025
law.effect: Substitutes the additional-dwellings table: 5% to £125,000, 7% to £250,000, 10% to £925,000, 15% to £1,500,000 and 17% on the remainder, for transactions on or after 1 April 2025.

autumn_budget_2024__sdlt_additional_dwel.intent: Installed current law already holds the enacted surcharge, so the frozen forward delta changes nothing. Reverse the five rates to the 3%, 5%, 8%, 13% and 15% they replaced, over the delta's own windows, and keep the certified world as the reform world.
limitations: FY2024-25 stays unscored, as in the frozen construction: the rates first differ at the 2025 annual lookup, so the part year from 31 October 2024 has no effect here.

law.title: Universal Credit Act 2025, section 1: Standard allowance for tax years 2026-27 to 2029-30
law.effect: Sets minimum standard allowance amounts: CPI growth, then uplifts of 2.3%, 3.1%, 4.0% and 4.8% for 2026-27 to 2029-30.

spring_statement_2025__uc_standard_allow.intent: Installed current law uprates the allowance by the index that applies the legislated uplifts, so the certified world holds them through 2029-30. The frozen counterfactual still runs unchanged, and each row measures current law against that path.
limitations: The counterfactual keeps the benefit-CPI path frozen on policyengine-uk 2.89.2, so later-year effects also carry any gap between that path and this engine's benefit index; CONSTRUCTION_PREMISES.json records the values this engine re-authors.
missing_legs: Existing/new-claimant health-element protections interact with the allowance change; this leg holds the certified health world fixed.
OBR Welfare outside cap is not separately identified by the annual UC liability; it has no invented mapping.
